captured_note: The inventory (docs/INVENTORY.md) classifies mar as submodule+adapter. The captured lab wrapper's `from models_mar import mar_base` is stale against the pinned upstream, whose module is `models.mar`; the port writes the correct import.
note: The model is the pinned upstream under third_party/mar, imported and never copied here (DESIGN section 1). The fork carries a two-line, device-preserving patch over base_commit: sample_orders() and forward_mae_encoder() built tensors with a hard-coded `.cuda()`, so MAR.forward() raised on a machine with no GPU; the fork uses the device of the model's parameters and of the input instead (identical to `.cuda()` on a GPU). This is DESIGN section 2.8's submodule+patch mechanism. The upstream training engine (engine_mar.py) is not used: it imports torch_fidelity and cv2 on import and calls torch.cuda.synchronize(), so it neither imports nor runs without a GPU; train_step1_mar.py owns the cached-latent path of its train_one_epoch with the DDP/AMP/EMA/FID machinery removed.
encoder: encoder.pt is the MAE-encoder side of MAR (z_proj, z_proj_ln, encoder_pos_embed_learned, encoder_blocks, encoder_norm, class_emb, fake_latent). The decoder and the diffusion loss head are excluded. Which representation a downstream probe should read from a generative model is a separate, deferred question (CONTRACT section 7); this port ships no linear_eval stage.
rewritten_during_the_port: the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream engine's DDP/AMP/EMA/FID machinery so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged
